title: Closing reflections and plans for Las Vegas
summary: He reflects on sixty years in music, playing with Everett Lee and Dean Dixon, and plans to stir up Las Vegas.

story.theme_name: Late-career reflections: awards, legacy and life lessons
story.community_name: Looking back: no regrets, what it all meant

blocks.x: You know, this has been a wonderful 50, 60, 62 years, I guess, and all the experiences I've had and the fun. I got some of my -- I was inspired and it was more gratifying for some of the things I did with Everett Lee and Dean Dixon, two of our greatest black symphony conductors. I played concerts with both of them. And coming to Las Vegas -- I came here not to retire. I came here with a new idea that I was going to go on, and I intend to go on. I intend to open up the situation here and I think it needs it. And I have -- a lot of my friends said, "You came to Vegas to retire?" "No, not at all." I came here to really stir it up. So, I'm going to play some good jazz and some good old bassoon in Las
Vegas, so I hope I'm successful.
